text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - Bund futures post a stable end to the day, with market sentiment underpinned by Bundesbankers' EMU comments, foreign interest supported by dollar strength. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 103.30, down 0.08 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilts off highs but slightly up on the session in quiet market with few domestic factors to provide direction. Outlook positive but dealers see little activity ahead of Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 112-03/32, up 03/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - March bond future spent another day in narrow range with traders awaiting Greenspan, U.S. and German jobs data. Some spread trading between France/Bunds early on and rolling over from March to June PIBOR, but otherwise quiet. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 132.12 up 0.14 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures slipped in late afternoon trading after Bundesbank council member Helmut Hesse was quoted as saying that a delay in the launch of EMU would force a renegotiation of the Maastricht Treaty. His remarks hit a market which had earlier picked after Italian February CPI figures came in line with market expectations. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.78 down 0.22 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries dipped, then recovered on home sales data Leading indicators rise 0.5 pct as expected, no impact. Greenspan begins speaking on CPI revisions before Congress. Upside limited by Greenspan's testimony on Wednesday, and the jobs report on Friday. Analysts see corrective activity after key supports breached. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-06/32, up 01/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.82 percent.

JAPAN - Key March Japanese goverment bonds (JGB) futures ended slightly higher after rebounding sharply in the afternoon due to purchases of cash JGBs by a major life insurer, traders said. The life insurer apparently bought cash JGBs with around seven-year maturities, traders said.In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.45, up 0.19 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
